sn12.19:0.3: The wise man [compared] with the fool.
sn12.19:1.1: Near Sāvatthī the Exalted One said:—
sn12.19:1.2: “For the fool, Monks, cloaked by ignorance and tied to craving, this body is formed in this way:
sn12.19:1.3: There is just this body and names-and-shapes without:— thus this pair. Because of the pair [there is] contact, just six spheres of sense. Touched by these, or by one of them, the fool experiences pleasure and pain.
sn12.19:2.1: For the wise man, Monks, cloaked by ignorance and tied to craving this body is formed in this way:
sn12.19:2.2: there is just this body and names-and-shapes without:— thus this pair. Because of the pair [there is] contact, just six spheres of sense. Touched by these, or by one of them, the wise man experiences pleasure and pain.
sn12.19:3.1: What, Monks, is there here that is different, distinctive, diverse between the wise man and the fool?”
sn12.19:3.2: “For us, lord, things have the Exalted One as their root, their guide, their resort. Well indeed were it if the meaning of this that he has spoken were to manifest itself in the Exalted One. Hearing it from him the Monks will remember it.”
sn12.19:4.1: “Well then, Monks, listen, give your mind thoroughly and I will speak.”
sn12.19:5.1: “The ignorance, Monks, wherewith the fool, whose body is so wrought, is cloaked, the craving whereto he is tied, that ignorance the fool has not thrown off, that craving is not withered away.
sn12.19:5.3: The fool has not lived the divine life for the right withering away of ill,
sn12.19:5.4: therefore the fool at the breaking up of the body is on his way to [another] body.
sn12.19:5.5: He being on his way thither is not set free from birth, nor from old age and death, nor from grievings, from lamentings, from ills, from sorrows, from despairs—
sn12.19:5.6: I say, he is not set free from Ill.
sn12.19:6.1: The ignorance, Monks, wherewith the wise man, whose body is so wrought, is cloaked, the craving whereto he is tied, that ignorance the wise man has thrown off, and that craving is withered away.
sn12.19:6.3: The wise man has lived the divine life for the right withering away of ill,
sn12.19:6.4: therefore the wise man at the breaking up of the body is not on his way to [another sense-] body.
sn12.19:6.5: He not being on his way thither is set free from rebirth, from old age and death, from grievings, from lamentings, from ills, from sorrows, from despairs—
sn12.19:6.6: I say, he is set free from Ill.
sn12.19:6.7: This, Monks, is how the wise man is different, distinctive, diverse from the fool, namely in that he lives the divine life.”
